Speaker Nunziata addressed Council as follows:

I would like to take a moment on behalf of Council to acknowledge the Indigenous Peoples of all the lands that we are on today. We do this to reaffirm our commitment and responsibility in improving relationships between nations and to deepening our own understanding of Indigenous peoples and their cultures. It is a moment to reflect on the importance of this land, which we each call home.

We acknowledge the land we are meeting on is the traditional territory of many nations, including the Mississaugas of the Credit, the Anishnabeg, the Chippewa, the Haudenosaunee and the Wendat peoples and is now home to many diverse First Nations, Inuit and Métis peoples. We also acknowledge that Toronto is covered by Treaty 13 with the Mississaugas of the Credit, and the Williams Treaties signed with multiple Mississaugas and Chippewa bands.

July 29, 2026

Mayor Chow, during the morning session of the meeting, gave remarks about the late Penny Elizabeth Lamy and welcomed Penny Lamy’s family and friends who were present in the Council Chamber.

Councillor Chernos Lin, during the morning session of the meeting, gave remarks about the late Sheldon Fainer.

Speaker Nunziata, during the morning session of the meeting, called upon the City Manager to recognize staff from the City of Toronto and its Agencies and Corporations on the planning and delivery of the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Toronto.

The City Manager addressed City Council and gave remarks paying tribute to the many staff from the City of Toronto, its agencies and corporations, and external partners who helped make the World Cup a success. The City Manager thanked staff, some of whom were present in the Council Chamber, and introduced a short video created by City staff to showcase the highlights of the World Cup in Toronto.

Mayor Chow addressed City Council and gave remarks to celebrate and thank all the staff and volunteers, as well as members of advisory bodies and Members of Council, who contributed to delivering the World Cup, on budget, and spoke about the legacy of the World Cup for the City.

Councillor Michael Thompson, during the morning session of the meeting, thanked the Mayor for her leadership in the successful delivery of the World Cup in Toronto.

Deputy Mayor Ausma Malik, during the morning session of the meeting, gave remarks to recognize the contributions of staff and City leadership on the planning and delivery of the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Toronto.

Councillor Morley, during the afternoon session of the meeting, advised members of Council that July 11 marked the 31st anniversary of the Srebrenica genocide and that, since 2020, the City of Toronto has proclaimed July 11 as Srebrenica Genocide Remembrance Day. Councillor Morley gave remarks to honour the memory of the Bosniaks who were killed and gave to each Member of Council a Srebrenica Flower, gifted by the Bosnian Islamic Association Gazi Husrev-Beg.

Councillor Saxe, during the afternoon session of the meeting, welcomed the City Scouts who were present in the Council Chamber.

Mayor Chow, during the afternoon session of the meeting, announced the official opening of the Affordable Housing Award of Excellence, with the inaugural honourees to be named next year, and displayed for Council the new award, crafted from stained glass.

Mayor Chow shared highlights from Wendy’s career and welcomed Wendy’s family—husband Don Lobb and daughters Nora, Emily and Heather—who were present in the Council Chamber. Mayor Chow congratulated Wendy Walberg, thanked her for her service and leadership, and presented her with a commemorative scroll.

Wendy Walberg addressed City Council.
